text:
Not the worst, not the best. SaaS ruined another great product. I just need simple money tracking that works.  Instead I get a $100 subscription for a growing bundle of features and service I don’t need. Plus annoying plugs for me to buy the founder’s book and constant begging to get my friends to also subscribe.

Unfortunately there are no alternatives I’ve found that do what I need.  So I begrudgingly remain a YNAB subscriber.

Budgeting Changes Lives - Not an Exaggeration. I won’t speak for everyone, but I can imagine this is what happens with many out there: when you have $x amount in your bank account, you think to yourself “this item/good/service costs less than the $x dollars I have in my bank, therefore I can afford it!” In reality, you have no idea what you can/can’t afford unless you budget. Take the time to understand your finances and you will bear the fruits of that simple labor. Once you budget effectively, handling your money becomes fun, tactful, smart, proactive, etcetera. You will actually be able to afford the true necessities and work towards the wants in your life by using this app and understanding how it all works. Watch a YouTube tutorial, anything to help you utilize this wonderfully created app, and your life will change.

Great tool. Using this app I was able to save $3000 in four months. It has helped me develop discipline to the point we’re now I don’t need it to help me manage my financial situation, but I keep it just to check in from time to time to make sure I’m on track.
Been a user for 6+ years now…. I’ve been a YNAB’er for about 6 years now. I figured it was time for a review! I’ll keep it simple: I’m here to stay. Great job, YNAB!

Phenomenal. This app is slowly but surely changing my life, and therefore my children’s future. I got into the horrible habit of emotional spending and this app literally stopped it in about a month. Seeing the impact all those (so called) small purchases were adding up to completely changed my outlook on how to deal with money. I will never go back to life before YNAB!!!! I literally will be paying for this app for the rest of my life, and teaching my children (and gosh, anyone who will listen) how to do financial life with YNAB. Don’t even bother with any other financial apps. Watch all the you tube videos. Do the 34 day trial, and watch your life and your brain change for the better!!!!!
AMAZING. Literally the most incredible budgeting app that I have ever used. Everyone has to use YNAB - I genuinely mean that.

nah. immediately asks for money. sucks, i saw a youtuber use it and was interested. if you like putting your card details into something before even having firsthand experience with it, this might be for you, i don’t know.

Best Budgeting App!!!. Allows you to do the “envelope” system/separate money without having multiple bank accounts!  Also allows you to get credit card rewards cash while always having the full balance to pay every month!  I never have to worry about having the money to pay off my credit cards - it’s all been budgeted with YNAB.

Bad bad. Had such a hassle deleting my subscription,

I was automatically signed up for?

Great app to track your finances. I have been using it for the last year and it is one of the best decisions I have ever took. It provides clarity in handling your finances and facilitates making a plan.
Highly recommended

More clicks, broken functionality. The app has gotten away from its roots of simple design and functionality. Things are starting to break now too…such as the ability to select multiple new transactions and “bulk” categorize them all at once. The “Categorize” button at the bottom/right is literally unresponsive

Great practical budgeting. I’ve tried many different budgeting methods and apps, and this is by far the most effective for me. Assigning dollars truly prevents that “I have the cash” intrusive thought when impulse buying. App receives constant and positive updates. Truly a game changer, with admittedly a little bit a learning curve at first.
Step Down. I have used YNAB for decades. It’s my gold standard for when I help young men get on strong financial footing.

Broken. I get double charges for things constantly so I have to go back and forth between my bank statements and the app to fix it all. Then a week later the money is off again. There are too many errors with this app to feel comfortable using it

Actually true. While there are some items I would add to this app, their tag line is right on target. I don’t worry about money anymore! I’ve tried other budgeting tools in the past and this one is the only one I’ve used that actually helps me feel better about my finances!

Financial Life Changer. YNAB is a financial life changer. It’s given me a better framework to talk about money with my spouse and make long term plans for big purchases with the security of knowing I’m still saving for all of life’s regular expenses. I love this app.
Just use excel. For the learning curve required to use this app, I’d rather use excel.

Long time User. I’ve been a long timer user and have my entire family on this app now. However, recent changes to import are so bad that I’m forced to leave a bad review. Currently consider switching to actual budget. There have been a long series of questionable changes, but the payee renaming on import is so bad I can’t fathom how they allow this to roll out.
Worth the $. Best tool I’ve found for the “digital” envelope approach to budgeting
Used to be great, doesn’t update. This app used to be great for tracking spending and making a budget but it now takes 12-24 hours to sync transactions.

Do Less With More (Clicks). Another app ruined by bored designers chasing trends. They’ve sacrificed reliability and ease-of-use for unnecessary UI updates, requiring more taps and clicks to do the same thing. I’m not sure I’m interested in paying more year after year just to fund an endless cycle of interface refreshes.
Finally, money makes sense. Making sense of finances for the everyday person is no small task. This program somehow makes it seem effortless.

Free Year for Students is Great, but there is 1 caveat.. I really enjoyed the free first year, and being able to do a trial run to see if the app worked for me.

Some things that I found difficult were the Mac OS interface, the & sign being written as ‘ ampersand’, and also the transactions seemingly took forever to come over. Even once they did, the reconciliation process seemed very tedious and ultimately made me not want to open the app because of all the tasks that were stacked up.

Great execution except for reports. This app is beautifully designed, is fast and syncs flawlessly across my family’s devices. 

The only major downsides are 1) everything is modeled around monthly budgeting (biweekly budgeting isn’t supported strictly speaking) and 2) the reports are very minimal.

Grateful. I’m grateful for this budgeting app. It has made managing money so much easier. There are times I get behind and with access to import transactions I can always stay up to speed with my finances.

Meh. I have a strict budgeting system that I do mentally. None of these budgeting apps are good enough. They are either lacking important features that help with organization or they over complicate budgeting like YNAB.
App. Syncing for bank is extremely slow and doesn't update. Sometimes days later and still doesn't update the right amounts and never matches your bank account! Don't buy not user friendly either!

Super Capable Budgeting App. This is the best subscription I have. YNAB helps my wife and me know exactly where our money is and what we can and can’t spend. It has a steep learning curve, but it is totally worth it. Give it 3 months. It’s not easy, but it transforms your relationship with money. You feel so much better spending money because you know you can. It is a budgeting app that’s built for real life.

New UI is Terrible. Please change the UI back to how it was. The buttons are not intuitive and it’s actually more clicks to enter a transaction. I don’t why you all keep changing the product to make it worse. It was fine a couple years ago, and now it seems like each update is a downgrade. Won’t be renewing my subscription unless you can fix it back

Year later update. Same satisfaction as last post.  I started YNAB & just did not grasp how it worked. Finally after 3 months walked away. Then 3 months later opened it up & started new. It is a hard concept @ first but after 3 more months & now 6 months I have a great budget that allows me peace of mind for now - future  & not living paycheck to paycheck. 
Just remember Rome was not built in a day.

Good app overall, needs more data. I like this app overall. Makes it easy to track expenses and makes budgeting easier. However, I often find it is lacking in retrospective data. “How much money did I spend this month in xy or z category, and how does that trend over time?” Technically, this data is possible to pull (at least some of it), but it’s not easy and it’s not part of the budget plan itself. I wish it was easier to access. But overall, if you struggle to budget, this is a helpful tool.

Do you ever listen to your users?. STOP making all of these stupid visual changes. I did not sign up with YNAB for you to change all the visual flags every single week. By far, this app is the worst app I have ever used. I only use the desktop app because the app that you force upon us is so badly designed that it is inferior to my workflow. Rather than ask us for ideas about what we would like to see, why don’t you just roll back all of the changes you’ve made over the past five years?
The best. I love this app. I have a clear picture of my financial situation.

Does the job, but kind of complicated to use. This app can be very helpful for budgeting, but if you’re new to it, it’s kind of complicated. It caters well to those getting out of debt, but not to those who use credit cards without carrying a balance. I didn’t see a tutorial, but if there is one, it should be more obvious. Genuinely LOVE that it notifies you of transactions that need to be categorized and that it summarizes your spending for you to reflect on.

Best investment. I have been using YNAB for 5+yrs and I can’t imagine not having it! I’ve started my friends and family on it and they’re hooked too. It’s helped me manage, plan, save, and keep my head above water during stressful times. Highly recommend to everyone no matter where you are in your journey!

In Control. YNAB has put me in control of my finances. Even if I don’t technically use it to stay on budget, it is essential to know where my money is going. And it’s extremely satisfying to get 30+ days ahead of my expenses.

Great but…. YNAB is mostly great as a budgeting tool. This latest update though broke a lot of buttons in the app. Tapping on ready to assign does nothing. Same with some other buttons. Please fix the app. iPhone 13 mini.

Worth the learning curve. I was BAD with money. Now I’m on top of it and setting/achieving savings goals all thanks to the way YNAB makes you think about money. You have granular clarity of all of your expenses and can customize categories and goals to your needs. Now, there was a learning curve. It took me about 4 months, maybe more, before I felt completely clear and on top of it. There are just some things that are confusing and/or you need to realize first. First and foremost: ALWAYS INPUT AN EXPENSE YOURSELF AT THE TIME OF THAT EXPENSE - waiting for the expense to show up automatically later will wind up screwing up your balances and budget - their automatic import system is not always perfect and can be very delayed, causing your budget to get out of whack if you’re not paying close attentions. And that leads to the second: ALWAYS PAY CLOSE ATTENTION. This is the magic of YNAB. If you are dedicated to leveraging it and learning it, then you will realize that this isn’t about making your financial life easier. Not a “set it and forget it” tool. ITS A TOOL THAT FORCES YOU TO OBTAIN A GRANULAR AND CLEAR VIEW OF YOUR MONEY. To be the master of your money. To help you pay closer attention to it. YNAB is merely a robust, and relatively easy (for what you get) tool to gain this clarity over your finances. You need to learn and be on top of it. And that’s the whole point. There are great YouTube videos out there with tutorials and also videos and seminars on the YNAB site. Plus the customer support has been satisfactory. Last thing I’ll say is, don’t be afraid to start fresh with a budget. To wipe it clean and go again. As I was learning about YNAB, I kept trying to salvage the budget as it got wonky from things that I didn’t properly understand. I started fresh in January with clarity and have been GREAT since. Hope this helps steer some of you to making the leap into YNAB. It’s categorically one of the best financial decisions I’ve ever made.

Thorough but demanding. While YNAB is a very comprehensive application for tracking and planning your financial activities, I found it a bit more overwhelming than I originally thought. It proved to require a lot more setup and maintenance for my needs. The interface is also very busy and can be a challenge to navigate. If you’re someone who has a desire to actively track every single penny’s movements, this may be for you. I simply don’t have the time to be in the app constantly replanning and categorizing my financial affairs and need something a bit more passive with simple, accurate presentation. Rocket Money is my next option.

Formerly great. More annoying these days.. This app used to be great and I used to love it very much. I wish the product team would stop trying to “improve” things all the time. It seems like I need to adapt to some new page or feature that only adds more steps to the process of adjusting my budget. Will probably follow the lead of a couple of my friends and switch to Zerosum soon, as it feels like good, old YNAB - at a cheaper price, nonetheless.

Worse every update. They’re making their budgeting app so easy a baby could use it! Useless for an adult trying to really understand their finances though. It’s gotten so bad over the last two years I’ve had it.

UI/UX on a downward trend. They’re introducing dating-app-style cards to swipe for approving and rejecting transactions. Huge failure. Transactions are rows of data that I don’t think get processed by your brain the same way a picture of a human being does. Idk that new screen just forces me to pause and think too long, and I panic because there’s no way out. I much prefer seeing the list of transactions, where I can decide how and when to deal with them. Not sure why they’re heading this direction, but thank goodness there’s an option to opt out.

Updates make it worse over time. This used to be a nearly perfect app. It changed my life. Over time, however, the app keeps updating and morphing into a bloated, cumbersome and unintuitive "budgeting" app. This last update made things like entering a transaction a pain, and requiring multiple swipes and taps instead of just a tap and having everything pop up like it used to. 
I might be fine with YNAB, don't need the bloat and gimmicks for $100 a year.

EXTRAORDINARY. I was skeptical of YNAB at first, but a few months in, I now feel EXTREMELY comfortable about my not feeling worried about my expenses.
As someone who lives on one source of income, YNAB made my budgeting far better than anything I could have done.
As far as app usability is concerned, there are no issues whatsoever. For an app as complex as YNAB with so many features, it is extremely user-friendly.
I LOVE YNAB!!!!

Garbage changes. They keep adding unnecessary taps, for no reason.  No way to revert back to a useful UI.  Avoid this product.  It’s no longer magical. 9/23/26 Again!!! More unnecessary changes!! More taps to do the same thing that used to only one tap!!!!!! So frustrating. This is a cult, not a software company.

App Falling Behind. Update after Dev Response:

Bank connections drop, go stale, or import days late. “Refresh” does not mean real-time data. YNAB’s own help text admits imports can take up to three days and that they only check for cleared transactions a few times a day. When something breaks, the prescribed fix is reset the connection, again. After enough resets the button is locked, support still points me back to the same loop, and my first review got a generic reply that never addressed freshness, provider failover, or why I have to babysit the feed.
Terribly Confusing. This app is awful
Increasingly childish design. Ive been a loyal web user for years but the design changes from the last year are increasingly difficult to use.
Essential. YNAB has been saving my financial life for years and the app experience keeps improving.

Best software.. Been using YNAB since the desktop only version! I love the way the software handles credit card payments and helps me save for all those one off expenses.  Every dollar we have earned gets a job!! It can be a learning curve at first, but if you stick with it for at least three months, the subscription will pay for itself. Use the help center and look for YouTube videos.
Fun with finance. I actually enjoy doing my numbers.
Keeps me in control. Best system for budgeting. Assign every dollar before you spend it.

Life Changing. I had tried budgeting in the past in different ways.  I felt like there was a learning curve with YNAB, but now I can’t imagine not using it.  It helps with prioritizing your money tremendously.

Change your life. Budgeting works if you want to change your life. In 10 years of using YNAB we went from being a total of $250,000 in debt to $950,000 in net worth. 

It takes time and commitment to change.
Well worth it. This app has helped me and my family so much with our budget! Love it! I’ve used it for 3 years now and we have the best handle on our finances ever. Thanks!

Changed my life. This budgeting app has changed my life. I love how organized it allows me to be. How I can set goals for each category. And how I know what to expect as the month goes on financially. I don’t know why every single person in the world doesn’t use this app.

Love this app but finally ran into a bad problem. I’ve used this app for a few years now and never had a problem with it. It was revolutionary in helping me learn how to budget and gain control of my finances. However, I finally ran into a problem with the app that has put me in a very bad financial position. The app for some reason unlinked all my accounts over the last few days and when I linked them again there appeared transactions not only from the last three days but also random transactions over the last month from many of my accounts. Because these random transactions didn’t go through in a timely manner, I grossly overspent, when I wouldn’t have otherwise. I still love the app, so 4 stars, but taking a star away for this problem it’s put me in

A Minor Complaint. I finally figured out how to transfer money between categories, and see monthly activity on my iPad app. This is not intuitive, and somehow I missed the change. It is also different from the iPhone. Otherwise, I’ve been using it forever, and it’s done a great job for me.
Wildly inaccurate and annoying to use. The title speaks for itself. I'm going back to using paper and an excel document...It's recommended by any accountant worth it's salt anyways.

Great App. This product is essential to me feeling in control of my money. It helps me be proactive and plan. It integrates well with banks and credit cards. 

Has been extremely empowering/freeing for my family’s finances. We have a plan for every dollar!

Worth Every Cent. I have been using YNAB for 8 years and had a subscription the entire time. Its integration with our bank accounts and our credit cards has made reconciling and budgeting SO much easier. 

It’s simple and easy to use, and, if you ever need help, their support has come through every time. 10/10 would recommend.

No historical transaction import!?!?. The biggest issue is that YNAB only starts pulling transactions from the day you connect your accounts. It doesn’t automatically import historical data, and manually bringing in past transactions is unnecessarily complicated.

That means if you want useful spending analytics or realistic budgets based on your actual habits, you basically have to wait a month or longer for enough data to build up. That feels outdated for a modern budgeting app. How are you supposed to set an informed grocery, dining, or utility budget without seeing what you’ve historically spent?

The UI is decent, but there also seem to be way too many features and sections for my needs. I wish the interface were more customizable so I could hide features I don’t use and focus only on budgeting, spending, and analytics.
YNAB ❤️. YNAB makes budgeting so easy. The app allows me access anytime. I can check any time to see if I should or should not spend, if need be. It’s wonderful and recommended highly.

Perfect Budgeting and Tracking for me. I have used YNAB for close to a decade at this point and it has been really helpful for budgeting and getting a picture of my financial picture. New features continue to roll out and it’s nice being able to customize all the categories I want in my budget.

Happy use for over a decade. I don’t generally recommend apps or products but I am a big fan of YNAB and truly think it has helped me get on top of my finances so that now—they’re right—I don’t worry about them. If you want clarity about where your money is going and how to manage it, I don’t know that there’s a better product out there.

Best Budgeting App. Have tried several other popular budgeting apps and they are all the same, hard to budget and stay on budget.  YNAB is completely unique in the budgeting and connections between my bank, credit cards and loans are seamless.  Going on my second year and still loving it.  Have more control over my spending and savings then ever before.  Recommend for everyone who hates budgeting.  Five stars ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

I’m in love! ❤️💵. Best Budgeting App! 

Helps me plan for the future. 

This app helps me see where I am at financially,
And gives me peace of mind all my bills are covered.
Money Cents. It’s a great feeling of power and calm knowing where your money is and where it’s going. I’ve saved for trips, paid off my car early, and live life with peace of mind.

Made me a millionaire. I’m not kidding. I have been using this app for 20+ years (since the desktop version). I was able to control my spending and save for a house and make monthly 401k contributions. I’m now a millionaire. 10/10. I’ll be able to retire with a paid off house and a steady income stream at 65.
Would be lost w/o this app. I love the YNAB philosophy, method, software and app. There is continuous improvement whenever there are issues.

A game changer!. Been using it for several years now . I switched from Quicken since it was not as efficient in helping with budget. YNAB is a game changer in allowing easy budgeting and planning ahead.
Too expensive. I really like YNAB but I think it’s too expensive.
Changed my life. This app was introduced to me by my sister Camille Knop. She was amazing at helping me set up my account and coached me through my first year!
The new design is awful.. Why on earth would you get rid of the beautiful design you had before to go to this ugly tan bloated version?

Not as good as it used to be. I’ve used the app for a couple of years and they have made some really good improvements along the way but unfortunately the negatives are starting to outweigh those. My primary complaint is that imports from my bank are constantly delayed. My bank will show a transaction as cleared two days prior but it doesn’t make it to the app in time to be of much use. I need as near real-time as possible or at least daily for it to inform my decisions.

Hidden amounts after latest update. I need to see when I’ve had to allocate more than usual for a category. I need to see that amount so I don’t keep doing it. Would really appreciate if there were a way to reenable the numerical value for every category, even the ones that have already been “fully spent”. I get the point of a clean view usually, but this is important. I want to see all the data.
Easy budgeting. Easy and portable budgeting. Super convenient

Wish I would have started YNAB 10 years ago. Love it and now my son is seriously considering YNAB soon. He’s watching YNAB videos and gathering his paperwork.
Update: Son has started his YNAB journey.

Love YNAB. I started using YNAB in 2019, and it had helped me in so many ways. It helped me save for my down payment on my house, and then save a realistic 6 month emergency fund by assigning money to future months. Assigning money to categories really helps me prioritize my spending as well as plan for upcoming bills, vacations, home improvements, and more. Having to assign every dollar a job means I decide in real time what the consequence of overspending on a category will do. What category will have to have money removed to cover overspending? I recommend YNAB to everyone, as someone who has never been able to use budgets that required me to manually input transactions because I would get behind on entering them and then get overwhelmed, having all my accounts integrated and automatically import transactions means I can finally actually keep up with budgeting. I could go on and on.

Randomly loses connection to your accounts. Repeatedly and randomly lost connections to accounts so unless you check it every day you’ll lose stretches of spending or deposits, what’s the point of a budget app that doesn’t consistently track your cash flow?
New plan UI is awful. Way less information density. So hard to  read

Decent but a few things that made it weird. Mostly a note. When I went to make a payment with rewards points on a cc they system didnt understand that I didnt make the payment fully from my bank. As an account the fact I didnt have control over my “books” was frustrating because the JE would have been extremely simple. Good app tho just not for me

I see the value in it but still hate it. For a new user this app sucks. It should not be this difficult to figure out how to use this app. We had way more control of spending the first month but simply trying to plan for the next month is mental torture.

Was better. Frequent UI changes and modifications to the original YNAB paradigm of budgeting make this hard to recommend for long term usage. App itself is still barebones after many years of “redesigns”. YNAB the company and its leadership need a reset.

Used for years. Wonderful application and great customer service. Saves me hours a month when we do finances at the start of every month.  

Everyone should be using this.
My favorite app. Life-changing

Best Budgeting App Out There!. When I was looking for a budgeting app/website to replace the old Intuit Mint, I looked at everything out there. Initially I was a little hesitant to give YNAB a try because it was a little overwhelming at first glance! I used some of the video resources available through the app as well as recommendations/walkthroughs available on YouTube and it completely changed my outlook. Since then, YNAB has proven to be the most effective budgeting app I’ve ever encountered and has become an indispensable tool in my life. I highly recommend this app to anyone looking for a reliable budgeting solution.

Good for Using Your Budget but Not Making It. I love YNAB; I’ve used it for a decade. Unfortunately the app keeps putting form over function and keeps hiding data behind extra taps or UI elements that look pretty in screenshots and demo videos. The only functional way to create a budget or assign out money is by using the web app on desktop instead. Day to day management and transaction logging is still fine on mobile even with the extra taps, but it seems like as the years go by I do less and less on the app and more and more on web, whereas I used to do my budget entirely on my phone.

Saving more than money. The Ynab system really has given me so much peace of mind, eased anxiety, clarified goals, and help me feel like while I can’t have it all, I have enough. Before my partner and I started using this app, I worried about rent every month. I felt like I was never saving enough, guilty every time I inevitably had to move money from savings to checking. Now, for the first time in my adult life, I know I can pay to get my car fixed or take care of a sick pet without going into debt. Now we can dream of the future in a concrete way— save to move, save to put money towards going back to school, even save to buy a new rug.  I have financial security I never imagined I could have with my current limited income.

The spending breakdowns and analyses are extremely helpful and intuitive to use and reflect on. I look forward to assigning money each pay day. Some features— like “cost to be me” are less helpful, since many categories I’ve created aren’t ones I use every month. I know for my partner, their banking makes them reconnect their banking more often than mine, and that’s a little annoying but not a deal breaker. When I import transactions directly from my bank, I’ve ended up with duplicates after the automatic imports update. Overall minor issues I will gladly take for the peace of mind Ynabs given me!

Need to prioritize current users. YNAB is a great app. If you’re new to it then you should download it and follow the system because it will change your life. 

That being said, you all need to pay attention to what your current users are asking for. If the user base is split on an issue, then make it a setting they can choose. Offer some customization. 

For example, we want biweekly targets. I’m not going into the details here as YNAB is well aware that customers want this and the subject has been beat to death on reddit and people (including me) have reached out to them directly. However they’d rather spend their time messing up the experience for people like me who have been using the app for almost 10 years. 

I’m specifically referring to how we now have to tap the search box to search the categories list when adding a transaction. This is a daily task that users have built into their muscle memory and now you’re changing it? Why? And you’re prioritizing this over the your customer’s requests for major feature upgrades like biweekly targets?

It’s fine if some people prefer to scroll rather than search. This brings up another area where YNAB is seriously lacking: customization. This isn’t the first time you’ve messed with the categorization workflow, which would suggest that your users are split on whether they like to search or scroll. Here’s an idea: make it a setting! Give us a choice! Stop trying to force a particular way on me! 

Another aspect that has degraded over the years is how we add categories and arrange the order they’re shown in the plan. I want my categories to be in order of when the bills are due. We used to be able to view the due dates for targets while reordering and adding categories but now I have to make sure to figure out where a category goes before I go to the screen to add it. Otherwise I have to leave that screen and return to the plan where I end up tapping on the individual categories and tapping “details” to check due dates, carefully figure out where a new category should live, return to the category add screen and tap “reorder” where I finally move it to its home. 

I guess I just want more customization. As it stands now, if another app were to offer YNAB any competition, I would happily jump ship.

Cleared Button Request. Please move the “cleared” button up instead of having to hit “show more” and scroll to get to it.  Something was changed a few months ago, and seems a small difference, but it makes entering transactions more cumbersome

Simple isn’t always better. The visual look is too minimalist. I’m use to seeing what I’ve contributed to each category thus far. Now I have to click into the category to check. 
While I enjoy minimizing my unnecessary spending adding unnecessary steps to stay on track is annoying. At least have a toggle for those who appreciate seeing that column.

Great app. This is a really effective tool and the app makes it very easy to keep up on your budget almost continually once you train yourself how to use it. It is fairly intuitive, but the YNAB system takes some time to learn and adopt.

Love the product but…. Been using YNAB for over a year now and it has honestly changed my finances dramatically. It did take a little while to learn but once I understood it, it allowed me to be more thoughtful about my money. I told all my friends because I think it’s that great. However, the app design changes over the last couple months are pretty frustrating. It seems like essentially they are adding extra taps for no perceived benefit. I am for all changes that things more efficient and easy to understand but these are not that. I would urge the developers to go back to earlier design principles of simplicity.
Get it!. Once you get the hang of it, it is a game changer for budgeting! I have been using it for many years. They keep making it better and better over time. I am a loyal YNABer.

Improve Your Life!. This app does more for us and our family than any other app and the educational material that goes along with it is invaluable.  We have been using it for about four years and there’s no app more essential to us!!

Much more than a budgeting app. YNAB is the only budgeting app that’s actually changed our financial life. Since 2020, it helped us buy a truck with cash, plan our next car the same way, and stay completely out of debt by turning future expenses into something we plan for instead of falling into unplanned spending. I feel like I’m being forced out as a user because clean informative presentation has been traded for  scrapbook styled presentation.

Every update makes it worse.. 4 years ago this was hands down the best budgeting app. Every few months they now update the app and EVERY single update makes the app worse. Woke. This app used to be about money. They added an LGBT etc angle. Not what I’m paying for. Just do your job.

I’ve been a subscriber for five years because YNAB’s budgeting philosophy is excellent. The best decision I’ve ever made…. I absolutely love this app. I literally am never stressed about money anymore. It’s addicting.
New updates. They keep changing things unnecessarily and upending a perfectly functioning UI. Time to start looking for a replacement.

Unwanted new changes. I’ve been using this app for over half a decade now. I loved the balance it struck between simplicity and more complex arrangements like saving for a vacation, etc. I hate several of the new changes. First, the beta testing being done currently where the progress bar has been replaced by circles — get rid of that, no one likes it. I also hate that the option to mark something as cleared is now hidden behind a “see more” button. Your UI designers should try actually using the app in day-to-day life before making changes that make it overall harder to use and a less pleasant experience. 

I love the premise of YNAB, and so far it has been working well for me, which is why I’ve stuck with it for so long, but if you keep making changes like this, you’re going to lose your established user base & word of mouth — the very things that led to your initial success.

Go back to the other version. Please please please go back to the previous version with the bars and not the circles! I will cancel my subscription because I hate this so much, it was so much easier to see how much I have left at a glance with the way it was before, get rid of those circles!!!!!!!! Bring back the line/bar view!!! I’m BEGGING you.

Pointless redesigns. I’ve been a long time customer and am now looking for alternatives because they keep redesigning the app for no reason.  It’s obvious that YNAB’s employees do not use the app themselves because otherwise they might understand the friction they’re adding to people’s workflows.

The most important task in a budgeting app is - if you can believe it - being able to see your budget and add transactions.  So what do the geniuses at YNAB do?  They make the default screen when the app opens a “Home Screen” that has neither of those things and instead has a list of tasks like a to do app.  

And now instead of a simple process bar representing how much is remaining in a budget, the budget screen now uses circular graphs for some reason.  I assume that they used AI to make this change at random because anybody who takes a moment to actually think would recognize that the old design (progress bars in uniformly fixed width rows) is a much more useful presentation of data.

YNAB was a great and useful product that is now an enormous chore simply because the people who make it are too lazy to try using their own app.

Stop making changes with no option to decline them. I don’t care if the team apparently wants to change the entire design and UI philosophy of the app, but having the option to maintain a “Classic”
view or similar should at least be an option. 

The way the budgets look now, the way it hides the budgeted total until you click on the budget line, is horrendous. The little icons on each budget item look busy, and overcomplicate the UI. Why do I want to see “Fully spent” repeated over and over again? Why add so much text to a line when a budget total told me everything I needed to know before?  Entirely removing the ability to see your budget lines at-a-glance is absurd. It feels like an overcorrection towards an ideal that no one but the YNAB team themselves wanted to make. It’s not user friendly, it’s dev friendly. 

I’m capable of rolling with the punches. I’m not one to howl to the heavens when things change. I’m adaptable, and understanding. But 2026 has been an awful year for YNAB updates. All-or-nothing UI updates, no customization to maintain consistency, an entirely useless “Home” page that pushes ads, redundant pages, murdering the design. It feels like kowtowing to a corporate ideal, not ensuring reliable service to users. 

This is an app that people use frequently throughout their daily lives. It is an app for budgeted finances, something that is stressful at a baseline, especially in the world economy today. You have to understand that an unexpected change to someone’s FINANCES is going to be extremely uncomfortable. This is a very personal thing you’re messing with. Why make bracing, irreversible changes with no recourse or options? It’s adding gasoline to a fire. 

Rein it in, guys. I’m glad you’re feeling yourselves and feeling confident, but your design team and philosophy is not more important than a feeling of reliability and comfort for your users. No user thinks about or cares about the vision of YNAB Inc. They want a comfortable place to manage their finances without disruption or surprise. Get over yourselves, be humble.

Needless Changes. Amazing!. Have been using it for 4 years now.  It has transformed my understanding on how to manage money.

The best budgeting app - second to none.. This app is the best you will find. Why am I clicking things more than I needed a month ago?. Do y’all actually use your own app because most of the stuff that gets changed should be counter intuitive to anyone who actually does.

Too much AI interference. I used to be able to trust YNAB as a rock solid budgeting and tracking app, in which any errors were made by me and easy to fix. Now it keeps surprising me with “helpful” AI interventions, then blaming me when I question them. The most recent was an “automatic reconciliation adjustment” that threw off my cleared balance by over $2000 while I was n vacation! When I looked into the reason for this I found out that the app (randomly) makes an adjustment when the cleared balance doesn’t match that of my credit union. In this case it created a huge error. There is no way to turn this function off and the answer given by the chatbot was to reconcile it myself more often. I had just reconciled two weeks before and this kind of interference is neither helpful nor necessary. I also frequently find duplicate transactions. It’s impossible to do zero dollar budgeting when the dollars are inaccurate. Please make these AI interventions optional!

True Budgeting Unlocked. I discuss money with people for a living. YNAB has helped me and my wife tremendously. We too have fallen into the “lifestyle creep” as we grow our professional careers. YNAB has helped us not only with tracking expenses, but also behavior modification. Making informed decisions with finances is so important. YNAB allows you to make financial decisions with confidence. I highly recommend this app to anyone who feels like they’re behind, needs clarity with their finances, or even is at a good place financially.

Best Budget App. I love YNAB! I have tried several budget apps but could never stick with it. YNAB works so well since it easily syncs with all my bank accounts and it handles credit cards extremely well. The notifications for new transactions are the reason I remember to stay on track, and the app looks modern and sleek and is a pleasure to use.

Best budget app ever. Been using YNAB for years and it has transformed our personal and business finances. Even our teens have their own YNAB budgets now and love it. Great customer service and easy to use. I recommend to everyone.

Farewell. After three years, I am switching to Copilot Money. On the one hand, YNAB did wonders for my finances. I have truly learned how to manage my credit cards and not carry a balance. Our savings and investments are up. Our bad debt is almost gone. But, it hasn’t been easy. A primary issue is manual and imported transactions not matching up. The interface is not user-friendly. I have wasted so much time trying to figure out why my figures are off and trying to set up my categories in a way that suits me. There are no color customizations and it needs a third tier of subcategories. The app has a section for videos and written material to explain how it thinks on the backend, but they are too general, never addressing the issue I was actually having. The people in the videos don’t get to the point. Rather than just giving me the answer I’m looking for, I have to watch a skit where they’re trying to turn it into a comedy show. The problems increasingly become worse with every major update that adds unnecessary functions, tabs, and other changes. Not only do they make the app more confusing, but they also add steps. For example, when transactions import, I can no longer manage those from the plan page. I have to go to the home page in order to review them. The review page used to be helpful. Now, it has useless features like a bar chart showing me that on average I’m spending less than I make, which you can’t even click on to get more detailed information. I’ve been asking for the same income and expense report that can be accessed on the website to be added to the app so that I could easily see my average spending per category per month in order to update my plan (a basic tenet of budgeting) to no avail. I no longer see income, and even when it was there, it lumped everything together.  Overall, what was a game changer for me just a couple of years ago, is now just cumbersome.

Not only have I contacted their customer service a multitude of times resulting in long drawn out exchanges that rarely fix the issue, but the last time they suggested that I don’t create manual transactions at all and just wait for them to import on their own. In other words, I have to budget on their time not mine and wait days until the import shows up! Even today yet another error. I made a credit card payment a couple of days ago and what is supposed to happen is that I will have a deduction from the account I paid from and a credit to the account I paid to. For unknown reasons, there were three transactions, and that third one doesn’t exist in the real world. This is not the first time that YNAB has created transactions that don’t exist. I had to go into three different accounts and make sure that somehow this didn’t actually happen. Then I had to delete the erroneous transaction and reconcile in YNAB. This is exactly why I’ve canceled my subscription.

Best thing since sliced bread. I make decent money and I should easily have plenty leftover at the end of the month to save. I look forward to assigning every dollar to a “ envelope” knowing I’m bettering my situation.
long time user. I've been using YNAB for years. It's worth every dime. Definitely helps me keep my finances sorted. If it could just help me make money that would be better.

YNAB Is The GOAT. I don’t do reviews, but I had to let everyone know that this is, hands down, the best app for taking control of your money and life. Worth the money, worth the learning curve. NEVER worry about money again.

Best Budgeting App I’ve used. I was jumping from budgeting app to budgeting app. I’ve been with YNAB for 5 years now and it’s great. I don’t want to swap budgeting apps again. 

A few notes for those interested: it follows the envelope budgeting philosophy. If you go by another budgeting philosophy strongly, then this app might not be for you. Also if you are tracking investments, this app doesn’t support that very well. I want to manually track my investments, since if they were all automated I would be as diligent at checking them. But some do more frequent trades or don’t want the hassle of manually tracking, so fair warning. 

Having said all that, I want to emphasize how broad and customizable this app is. Even with the envelope philosophy there is so much you can customize. I really love this app.
Corrections. Wish there was a way to see a list of recent entries, so that if there was a mistake made during a session of making multiple entries i could review to see, and correct, the error.

Changed my life. I’ve gone from living in a state of fear about how or if I was going to be able to pay next month’s bills to having multiple streams of savings and being months ahead on bills. I’ve never been so financially secure in my life, thanks to YNAB.

Game changer!. Definitely recommend it to anyone that is committed to their financial goals. It takes a little more work at the beginning but so worth it! We like to talk to our friends about how good this app is!!

YNAB has changed my life. Let me start off by saying that I’ve never been able to stick to a budget. Despite having a lot of financial anxiety for almost my entire life, I’ve always struggled with making a budget and sticking to it. For most of my adult life, I’d go though this cycle of sitting down for a few hours and making a budget, swearing to stick by it, then forget about it until a few months later when I was short on money. I felt like I was working and making good money and not spending frivolously, but somehow couldn’t seem to save or build wealth. Then I found YNAB. This app has completely changed the way I think about money and has helped me save thousands of dollars in just 6 months. Furthermore, YNAB has afforded me the everyday peace of mind that comes with knowing I have money set aside for every need/category. Also, for folks with ADHD this app will not only make you aware of forgotten subscriptions, etc. but it also gives you little dopamine hits when you get paid and allocate your money to different categories. It sort of gamifies budgeting! I will say, it takes a while to get used to the system (1-2 months for me) but if you put in the time and watch some tutorials on YouTube it’s life changing. Thanks YNAB!!!

Free Trial. I don’t normally write reviews, but one thing about this app that I genuinely appreciated was the actually free “free trial”. I didn’t have to worry about trying it out, forgetting if I needed to cancel and accidentally getting charged. I got to use the app, test features, and see if I liked it with peace of mind, something I wish more companies would do. Great app!
Smooth app experience. Very clean UI that makes our money management a breeze. It’s super helpful to reference transactions from a year ago, or to add new transactions.

Game Changer. There is a steep learning curve to really get the most out of this app, but once you get it, it is actually super easy and SO worth it. I used Nick True’s YNAB beginners video on YouTube. I went from feeling like I live paycheck to paycheck (because I had no visibility on my spending) to realizing that I have money to spend and save for my goals, I just needed to be more organized. Now I am working on getting one month ahead and I feel confident in my finances rather than restricted like most budgets.

Support is responsive & constant improvements. When I first signed up for the trial month of this app to see if I could use it instead of the EveryDollar budgeting app, there were some glitches that were making it hard for me to decide which app was best. But I mentioned those glitches in my first review of the app and within a short period of time they’ve been resolved. 

This app is so versatile and well designed to keep track of credit card expenses to make sure you know how much you have spent versus how much you have in the bank. In fact, the desktop version of the app is so versatile that it has a bit of a steep learning curve, but I love that because it provides so much more room for configuring the budget to one’s unique needs and circumstances. 

Where this app is particularly a winner over the EveryDollar app is its ability to integrate credit card expenses and on the desktop app you can see the monthly total funds available that is accurate. The EveryDollar number for funds available is never accurate. (It only adds up what was budgeted for that month not what is actually available in each fund.) 

Very grateful to find this app. It’s perfect for our needs.

Best budgeting program on the market.. If you have any bookkeeping or accounting background, this is by far this the best personal budgeting program I’ve come across.. incredibly flexible. It’s allowing me to create our own little family bank. I love YNAB.
Helps you not stress about money any more!!. YNAB is worth the subscription for sure

Makes me feel free!. I don’t know I had an OCD itch that needed scratching until I found YNAB. Haha. When I started getting serious about budgeting this helped immensely.

It took me 6 months to really dial it in and figure out how much to allot to my categories. Grocery budget, no idea!  But tracking it let me find that number.  Now what YNAB does for me is give me freedom.  

I love having goals and categories to save for. Now when I want to take a trip I know exactly how much I can spend and it’s guilt free!  I know I won’t wreck my budget in another area and have the power turned off by not paying the electric bill. It’s an easy way (once you set it up) to plan for the future.  You get out of this app what you put in!

Out of Debt, No Longer Worried About Money. My wife and I have been using YNAB for more than twelve years. It helped us get out of debt, stay out of debt, and build our retirement accounts. The app lets my wife and I coordinate our spending. We know what expenses are coming and can set aside money accordingly. When we started, money was tight and unplanned expenses went on the credit card. Now we live on last month’s income and use our credit cards like a debit card. The money needed to pay them off monthly is always in our accounts, because YNAB tracks how much we have spent and deducts it from the appropriate categories, effectively setting aside the cash we will need.

Money Saver. I have been using this app for 3 years now. Since the first year, it has paid for itself. This is an easy way to watch how you spend money, see your money grow, and it helps you make decisions at the right moment. 
  If I go to a store and see something ‘shiny’ that I want. I immediately open up YNAB. Can I buy this, should I buy this, do I really need to buy it? 
  This app has made me accountable and allowed me to not only protect my spending but change my spending habits. Buy it. Set it up. Realize the hard truth about your spending habits. Become better with your own financing. It pays for itself and they are always improving the app. No brainer app.

Runs my life!. I’ve been using YNAB for years now, and I would be lost without it. I like to run a lot of things through credit cards to rack up points in. This really helps me stay on top of how much money I actually have and how much I’m putting on a credit card.

Finally consistent on budgeting. I underwent a big lifestyle change and ended up with a lot less income. I tried other apps but they were either too complex or too manual. I hated the idea of a budget and used shopping as a stress reliever. When I started about 1 year ago my net worth was negative -$3000. Through the app I was able to pay down debts and make a budget I could stick with. My net worth is now a positive $7000. I actually enjoy going in and doing my budget, I plan for annual bills, and I have an emergency fund started. I don’t stress about money (very often) and if I have an unexpected expense I know where I can pull from to cover it. Highly recommend!

Gold standard budgeting app. I’ve been using YNAB since before it was a subscription service - it has saved me tens of thousands of dollars and dramatically changed my mental framework around my finances. My financial preparedness for all expenses - small, big, daily, yearly, surprise, emergency, etc - has improved significantly since using this app and associated budgeting mindset. The subscription for YNAB more than pays for itself. I highly recommend it for anyone looking to reframe the way they approach their financial preparedness and future expenses!
Great App. Keeps you accountable and able to track your money. Can’t lie to yourself about what you’re spending.

I had already racked up a significant amount of credit card debt and had no idea how I would be paying bills that month. I had been reckless with my money, irresponsible…and I knew I needed to change.

So I took a long time researching what I could about finding the right app. I used the Dave Ramsey one for a while (Every dollar) and I used the Experian one for a while, but neither worked. There were limitations on managing the cash flow and carryover and management of actual categories. That is when I landed on YNAB.

I’ll be honest, at first I wasn’t impressed. The app had a lot going on and it took me a lot of time trying to figure out what every button does and what every term means. But for someone with variable income, this app has taught me to manage every new dollar that enters my bank account. I can see in real-time how my money is helping me pay off my debt, and rebuilding my savings. I can monitor what I’m putting towards my retirement accounts and ensuring I have the money when my bi-annual car insurance payments hit. I can plan for a vacation with no stress, because I know that when the money is needed at those times I already have it set aside and not to be touched. The mental and emotional freedom I’ve been given by using a clear and accurate budgeting app has genuinely changed my financial future and my life, and I don’t know if I would have had this much peace without the help of YNAB. 

Their support is also amazing and everything you could ever ask about their app is in their Knowledge Base. I truly have no complaints!

Most other apps just tell you what you did in the past, which is not helpful in guiding your next purchase. As a result of YNAB, my paychecks now fund NEXT month. I bought my new car with cash. My vacation to Europe was paid in full ahead of time. All hail YNAB!
